result.title: RAGE: Residual-Adaptive Gating for Flow-Based Image Editing
result.summary: Recent inversion-free, flow-based image editing methods evolve the source image toward the target via a differential velocity field. We observe that this velocity field does not explicitly account for which regions should be preserved, leading to unintended drift in non-editing regions. To address this, we formulate source fidelity control as a stochastic optimal control problem in which a selective fidelity term on the editing residual is enforced along the editing trajectory. Solving this problem and approximating its solution yields the Residual Gating Principle: each latent component is pulled back toward the source with a gain that decays exponentially with the local residual magnitude, so that small deviations are suppressed while large, semantically meaningful edits pass through unimpeded. The proposed method, RAGE, requires only one lightweight gated interpolation per sampling step, involves no mask estimation, attention maps, retraining, or architecture-specific modifications, and is applied on top of FlowEdit-based editors. On PIE-Bench, RAGE achieves the best overall rank among 17 methods and substantially improves background preservation on both Stable Diffusion 3 and FLUX backbones while maintaining competitive editing quality.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文针对无反转、基于 flow 的图像编辑中非编辑区域漂移问题，将源保真控制表述为沿编辑轨迹施加残差选择性保真项的随机最优控制问题，导出「残差门控原理」：每个 latent 分量按局部残差幅度指数衰减的增益被拉回源图，从而抑制小偏差、放行语义性大编辑，并以每步一次轻量门控插值实现 RAGE。
AI.relevance_reason: 其逐 latent 分量、按残差幅度调制的回拉增益本质上是一种状态更新规则，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态该保留哪些视觉细节、何时允许改写提供可核查的门控线索，但该工作属图像编辑、不涉及推理，联系需自行核查。
